Uses of Interface
org.smtlib.ISolver

Packages that use ISolver
Package
Description
org.smtlib
This package contains the main classes and abstract interfaces for this SMT-LIB tool; the tool provides a stand-alone SMT-LIB-compliant command-line application, an application that responds to SMT-LIB commands over a network port, and an SMT-LIB Java API.
org.smtlib.command
This package contains implementations of the SMT-LIB commands, implementing the interfaces defined in ICommand; these implementations are independent of the concrete syntax that might be used, except that each command object has methods that can parse or print representations of the command in the standard (or potentially other) concrete syntaxes.
org.smtlib.ext
This package contains commands that are extensions to SMT-LIB.
org.smtlib.impl
This package is an implementation of the interfaces defined in org.smtlib.
org.smtlib.solvers
This package implements various instances of org.smtlib.ISolver, which are specific solvers that wrap and interact with various off-the-shelf SMT solvers currently available.

    Classes in org.smtlib that implement ISolver
    Modifier and Type
    Class
    Description
    class 
    AbstractSolver
    This class implements the operations of the org.smtlib.ISolver interface that map directly onto a single translated command sent to the solver process, with the expected response of a fully SMT-LIB compliant solver (a flat success/error/sat/unsat/ unknown/unsupported, or a bare value/attribute-pair for get-option/get-info): the command is translated with AbstractSolver.translate(INode) and sent via AbstractSolver.sendCommand(ICommand).

    Methods in org.smtlib that return ISolver
    Modifier and Type
    Method
    Description
    ISolver
    SMT.Configuration.createSolver(String solvername, String executable)
    Resolves the given solver name and executable to a concrete ISolver adapter instance, applying the same name/executable/adapter resolution jsmtlib.properties supports as SMT.startSolver(org.smtlib.SMT.Configuration, java.lang.String, java.lang.String) -- platform-specific .adapter/.exec overrides checked before their bare counterparts, the Solver_<name> naming convention, the z3-specific Solver_z3_recent fallback for an unrecognized z3 variant, the generic Solver_smt fallback, the "test" pseudo-solver special case, and %exec% command-array placeholder substitution -- but, unlike startSolver, this method does not start the solver and does not do any CLI-flavored error()/usage() reporting: any resolution or construction failure is reported as a thrown ISolver.CreationException instead, leaving it to the caller to start the returned solver (via start()) and decide how to report a creation failure.
    ISolver
    SMT.startSolver(SMT.Configuration smtConfig, String solvername, String executable)
    Starts the solver with the given name and executable, preset according to the given configuration.

  • Uses of ISolver in org.smtlib.solvers

    Classes in org.smtlib.solvers that implement ISolver
    Modifier and Type
    Class
    Description
    class 
    Solver_altergo
    This class is a FIRST-PASS, CI-UNVERIFIED adapter for Alt-Ergo (2.6.3).
    class 
    Solver_bitwuzla
    This class is an adapter for Bitwuzla (bit-vectors, floating-point, arrays and uninterpreted functions -- no arithmetic logics, no datatypes).
    class 
    Solver_cvc5
    This class is an adapter for cvc5, on the assumption that it is (or should be) a fully SMT-LIB compliant solver: it is a concrete, silent inheritor of AbstractSolver — only the startup command line (cvc5 needs --incremental to accept push/pop at all, and --quiet to suppress informational stderr chatter that would otherwise fool SolverProcess's stdout/stderr-preference heuristic) and Solver_cvc5.start() (process lifecycle) are overridden.
    class 
    Solver_simplify
    The adapter that drives the Simplify solver.
    class 
    Solver_smt
    This class is an adapter that takes the SMT-LIB ASTs and translates them into SMT commands over a solver process speaking plain SMT-LIB, for a solver assumed to be fully SMT-LIB compliant.
    class 
    Solver_smtinterpol
    This class is an adapter for SMTInterpol (a Java SMT solver launched as java -jar smtinterpol-VERSION.jar, not a native executable): it is a concrete, silent inheritor of AbstractSolver -- the base launch command is declared in jsmtlib.properties via org.smtlib.solver_smtinterpol-2.5.command (see SMT.startSolver's %exec% placeholder substitution), so only the conditional timeout flag and Solver_smtinterpol.start()/AbstractSolver.exit() (process lifecycle) are handled here.
    class 
    Solver_test
    This class is a Solver implementation that simply type-checks formulae and checks that commands are used correctly; it does not do any proving.
    class 
    Solver_yices2
    This class is an adapter that takes the SMT-LIB ASTs and translates them into yices2 commands
    class 
    Solver_z3_4_3
    This class is an adapter that takes the SMT-LIB ASTs and translates them into Z3 commands
    class 
    Solver_z3_4_3_2
    This is a special handler for Z3 4.3.2, as opposed to other revisions of Z3 4.3.
    class 
    Solver_z3_recent
    This class is an adapter for recent z3 versions (empirically verified against 4.8.12 and 4.10.2), on the assumption that they are (or should be) fully SMT-LIB compliant: it is a concrete, silent inheritor of AbstractSolver -- only the startup command line and Solver_z3_recent.start()/AbstractSolver.exit() (process lifecycle) are overridden.
